_doc: Townsfolk trading with each other (systems/townTrade.js). Every good and coin moves between named holders: the market's stock, a household's larder, a producer's wares, a pedlar's pack; the buyer's purse, the town's purse, the seller's purse. Nothing is made or lost but what is eaten, worn out or spoils.
_stepDays: Off the map every town with a roster trades every stepDays (staggered by place): the households eat from their larders, the producers bring their goods to market, the households shop, neighbours barter, pedlars sell door to door.

household._doc: A household keeps a larder of what its people use (the market's per-head need: data/markets.json perCapita x the town's demand) and shops to keep coverDays of it. Children eat childShare of a grown share. minLot: the smallest lot sold (a hundredth of a market unit). The poor (the household's purse under poorBelow) buy only the groups in poorGroups; below hungryCover of their food eaten in a dearth they go hungry (person.hungry, read by systems/townJobs.js); out of a dearth a household that can't buy is fed as before, by the town's stores, alms and plainer fare (the market's own eating).
household._cover: days of use kept by group: what lasts is bought in bigger lots, less often (a month of candles, a season of clothes, tools till they wear out)
household._reserveDays: what lasts (clothes, tools, candles, drink…) is bought only from coin over reserveDays of the household's food and fuel at today's prices: bread before boots

haggle._doc: Every purchase is haggled: the price paid is the stall's price x (1 +/- spread), by a hash of the buyer, the good and the day. A trip's first bargain driven past souredAbove of the spread may sour the buyer on the seller (sourChance): a grudge (systems/brawls.js feuds, reason 'cheated') and a 'cheated' line in the buyer's life.

cheats._doc: A crooked seller (crookedTraits, or the share of the rest by a hash) now and then (chance, on a household's trip to market) gives short weight: the buyer gets (1 - short) of what was paid for, and the overcharge goes into the seller's purse. Caught (caughtChance), the market warden refunds the buyer and fines the seller fineMult x the overcharge into the town's purse; uncaught, the buyer may notice later (noticeChance): a grudge.

wares._doc: Producers keep a little of what they make at home (their wares: what they sell a neighbour, the player, or cry in the street). At each market turn the named hands keep back perHand units a day of their share of the town's output (at most maxShare of what the town made of it that turn); at their next step whatever is over `keep` goes to market. New producers start with their keep from the market's stock where it can spare it.

barter._doc: Before the households go to market, one with something to spare (wares, or a larder over its target) calls on a neighbour: they swap goods for goods of the same worth (eggs for bread) — what the other has over and the first lacks; with nothing to swap, in a coin town the neighbour buys what they lack of it, purse to purse. pairs: calls a step; chance: per try in a coin town, inKind in a barter town (world/barter.js), poorBonus when either household is poor. Each swap warms the two households (ties) and cools a grudge between them.

pedlars._doc: Pedlars walk the roads between towns with a pack of real goods bought at one town's market (paid into its purse) for a town with a roster, sell door to door a little under the stalls' price (undercut), and sell what's left to that town's market before moving on with a new pack. A pedlar's purse is first drawn from the purse of the town they set out from, and is left to the town where they give up the road. everyDays: a town with a roster sees one when none has come for this long.

merchants._doc: A merchant caravan leaving a town with a roster is a named merchant's venture (one of its merchants): the caravan carries their name, their life remembers it (once per logEvery days).

shops._doc: The street map's merchants, travelling traders and smiths (systems/npcShops.js; the roll of what each deals in: world/innerMap/state.js _generateNpcShop; the menu: ui/actionMenu/trade.js showNpcTradeMenu). Their goods are real: a trader on the town's roster sells their own wares first (the coin to their purse), then the town market's stock on consignment (the coin to the town's purse, commission of it to theirs); a trader with no roster record sells the town market's stock; a travelling trader sells their home town's (a neighbouring town by who they are, else this one). The shop shows the roll's quantity capped at what the source has above keepShare of the market's target. A good no market trades is dealt as its standIn, else not at all. Bought from the player: only goods a market trades, into that market's stock, paid out of that town's purse as far as it has the coin. A town that barters sells nothing on consignment and buys nothing for coin.

onMap._doc: The street map: shoppers at a stall buy what their larder wants (world/innerMap/townTrading.js), carry a sack home; producers take their wares to market at dawn; bakers, fishers and brewers cry their wares in the street of a morning; neighbours stop to swap; a pedlar in town walks the streets crying his pack. Chances per pick of an hour's business.

buy: Same as yesterday. Dearer than tomorrow.
I'll have some {good}. Fair weight, mind.
For you, a fair price. For him, double.
Is that the best you can do?
It's the best anyone can do. Take it.
dear: You'll ruin me at these prices.
Last week it was half that!
broke: Not today. My purse is light.
I'll come back when I've the coin.
Too dear for me, I'm afraid.
cheated: That's short weight! I paid for more than this!
Your scales lie, and so do you!
fined: The warden's fined {name} for short weight!
Short weight at {name}'s stall: fined, and serves them right.
barter: I've {give} to spare. Have you any {get}?
Go on, then. You drive a hard bargain.
deliver: First at the stalls, best price.

bread: Hot bread! Fresh from the oven!

pedlar: Needles and pins, ribbons and salt!
Pots and candles, soap and spice!
What d'you lack? I've a little of everything!

sell.ask: Will you sell me some of your {good}?
sell.done: Done. Mind you use it well.
sell.none: I've nothing to spare, I'm afraid. It's all spoken for.
sell.noCoin: We've no coin here, friend. Bring goods to swap.
sell.poor: That's more than you can pay.
